title: OpenAI Offers Zero Data Retention for Frontier Models in Challenge to Anthropic
excerpt: New privacy technology lets OpenAI detect AI misuse across interactions without retaining customer data, as the company targets enterprises frustrated by Anthropic's 30-day retention mandate.
body:
• OpenAI announced Zero Data Retention for its frontier models, pledging not to store customer prompts or responses — a direct challenge to Anthropic's mandatory 30-day data retention policy.
  • A new system called Private Safety Processing lets OpenAI detect misuse patterns across interactions without giving its employees access to the underlying content.
  • The move has drawn support from enterprise customers in regulated industries and criticism of Anthropic from figures including David Sacks, Satya Nadella, and Alex Karp.

OpenAI Draws a Line on Data Privacy

OpenAI on Wednesday unveiled a significant expansion of its Zero Data Retention (ZDR) program for enterprise customers, announcing that it will not store prompts or model responses from businesses using its AI models. The company also previewed a new technology called Private Safety Processing that lets it monitor for misuse across multiple interactions without giving OpenAI employees access to the underlying content, according to The Wall Street Journal.

The announcement is a calculated competitive move against Anthropic, whose policy of retaining customer data for 30 days to monitor the safety of its latest models — including its Mythos-class systems — has drawn growing criticism from enterprise customers and Silicon Valley leaders.

"We've heard very loud and clear from businesses that this is important. They often have their own commitments that they have made to their customers if you think about somebody who is serving other enterprises, who are trusting them with incredibly sensitive data."

— Aleah Houze, OpenAI Head of Product Policy

How Private Safety Processing Works

The technical challenge OpenAI is addressing is real: as AI models take on longer, more complex tasks, safety risks that span multiple interactions are harder to detect from a single prompt. Anthropic has argued that its 30-day retention is necessary to catch these patterns.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PpgPh8z_4tM

OpenAI's answer is a system where customer data stays on infrastructure controlled by the customer, or on OpenAI infrastructure encrypted with customer-controlled keys. Automated systems scan for patterns indicating misuse — such as cyberattack coordination or biological weapon research — and send OpenAI only a narrow signal indicating the type and severity of the risk. OpenAI employees never see the actual prompts or responses, even when content is flagged.

Customers can investigate alerts through their own systems and choose whether to share additional information with OpenAI if they want to appeal a decision or support an abuse investigation. OpenAI said Private Safety Processing is currently being tested with early customers, with a broader rollout and technical white paper planned for September.

The Competitive Context

The data retention debate has become a flashpoint in the AI industry. Anthropic's 30-day retention policy for its Mythos-class models applies "on every platform where these models are offered," according to an analysis by PCTech Magazine — meaning even enterprise customers with existing zero-retention agreements may not be able to opt out for those specific models.

White House AI adviser David Sacks said in June that Anthropic's retention policy was "creating a new level of AI haves and have-nots." Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and Palantir CEO Alex Karp have also argued that businesses need certainty that AI companies are not retaining their data, particularly in regulated sectors like healthcare and finance.

The friction comes at a notable moment. OpenAI recently told investors that its second-quarter revenue growth lagged behind Anthropic's, according to the Journal. Anthropic's popularity with businesses paying for its coding tools and advanced models has given it significant enterprise momentum, making OpenAI's privacy push both a principled stance and a business necessity.

What It Means for Enterprise AI

For organizations handling sensitive data — financial records, health information, legal documents, proprietary research — the difference between zero retention and 30-day retention is not academic. It affects regulatory compliance, contractual obligations with their own customers, and risk assessments that security teams build their architectures around.

Glean CISO Sunil Agrawal, quoted in OpenAI's announcement, said the company's "no-training commitment and ZDR give Glean confidence to build with OpenAI," adding that "safety can advance without compromising the privacy and control that sustain enterprise trust."

The announcement does not resolve every concern. Even under ZDR, flagged content can still trigger enforcement actions, and metadata like API keys, timestamps, and token counts is still logged. But for enterprises evaluating which AI provider to build on, the gap between OpenAI's approach and Anthropic's has become a concrete differentiator.
